newsitem.title: USA: California Senate panel clears school bond reform.
newsitem.headline: California Senate panel clears school bond reform.

text.p: A California legislative panel on Wednesday approved a bill that would make it easier for school districts and community colleges to issue bonds.
The state Senate Constitutional Amendments Committee voted 3-to-1 to approve Senate Constitutional Amendment 12, by Senator Jack O'Connell, a Democrat. The bill now advances to the Senate floor.

If approved by the legislature and the state's voters, the measure would roll back California's restrictive two-thirds voter requirement for general obligation bonds issued by school districts and commmunity colleges.
Under O'Connell's measure, local general obligation bond issues for school construction and improvements would require the approval of a simple majority of the voters.
The measure would also remove the cap on property taxes used to repay bonds to finance school improvements.
Supporters of the measure said the reforms would provide a significant funding boost to school districts.
Since 1984, 490 school districts have placed local school bond measures on the ballot. Only 48 percent received the two-thirds vote required for approval of local bonds.
If a majority vote were required for approval, 92 percent of the local bond measures would have passed, according to a Senate analysis of O'Connell's bill.
